title: How to Log Meals on Zepbound: Complete Tracking Guide
summary: Learn how to log meals on Zepbound effectively with this expert guide. Discover the best tracking apps, essential nutrients to monitor, portion measurement techniques, and common mistakes to avoid while taking tirzepatide for weight management.
body_text: Tracking meals while taking Zepbound (tirzepatide) is essential for optimizing treatment outcomes and monitoring nutritional adequacy during weight management therapy. As a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, Zepbound significantly reduces appetite and alters eating patterns, making systematic food logging a valuable clinical tool. Proper meal documentation helps ensure adequate protein intake, identifies potential nutrient deficiencies, reveals food tolerance patterns, and provides objective data for healthcare providers to guide treatment decisions. This comprehensive guide explains practical strategies for logging meals effectively while on Zepbound, including recommended tools, essential nutrients to track, and common mistakes to avoid for safe, successful weight management. Quick Answer: Meal logging on Zepbound involves recording all food and beverage intake immediately after consumption using a tracking app or journal, documenting portions, protein intake, meal timing, and any gastrointestinal symptoms to optimize treatment outcomes and monitor nutritional adequacy. Zepbound (tirzepatide) is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist FDA-approved for chronic weight management that reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying Systematic meal tracking helps monitor adequate protein intake, identify nutrient deficiencies, and document food tolerance patterns during treatment Record all intake immediately after eating including portions, timing, hunger levels, and any gastrointestinal symptoms using consistent measurement tools Track protein intake targeting 1.0-1.2 grams per kilogram body weight daily, along with macronutrient distribution, fiber, and hydration status Contact healthcare providers promptly for severe vomiting, inability to retain fluids for 24 hours, severe abdominal pain, or signs of dehydration We offer compounded medications and Zepbound®. Compounded medications are prepared by licensed pharmacies and are not FDA-approved. References to Wegovy®, Ozempic®, Rybelsus®, Mounjaro®, or Saxenda®, or other GLP-1 brands, are informational only. Compounded and FDA-approved medications are not interchangeable. Table of Contents Understanding Zepbound and Why Meal Tracking Matters Step-by-Step Guide to Logging Meals While Taking Zepbound Best Apps and Tools for Tracking Food on Zepbound What to Record: Nutrients, Portions, and Timing Common Meal Logging Mistakes to Avoid on Zepbound Frequently Asked Questions Understanding Zepbound and Why Meal Tracking Matters Zepbound (tirzepatide) is an FDA-approved medication for chronic weight management in adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity. As a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 ( GLP-1 ) receptor agonist, Zepbound works by reducing appetite, slowing gastric emptying, and may improve glycemic measures, especially in people with type 2 diabetes. These mechanisms significantly alter eating patterns and nutritional intake, making systematic meal tracking a recommended component of treatment. Meal logging while taking Zepbound serves multiple important purposes beyond simple calorie counting. First, it helps patients and healthcare providers monitor adequate protein intake, which becomes particularly important as appetite decreases and weight loss accelerates. Insufficient protein consumption may contribute to lean muscle mass loss, potentially affecting metabolic health. Second, tracking identifies potential nutrient deficiencies that may develop when overall food volume decreases substantially. Third, documentation reveals patterns of food tolerance, as some patients experience gastrointestinal side effects including nausea, vomiting, and constipation that may vary with meal composition and timing. Systematic meal logging also provides objective data for clinical decision-making. When patients report side effects or inadequate weight loss, detailed food records enable healthcare providers to distinguish between medication-related issues and dietary factors. The American Diabetes Association emphasizes that pharmacotherapy for weight management achieves optimal results when combined with lifestyle interventions, including dietary modification. Meal tracking creates accountability, increases nutritional awareness, and facilitates the behavioral changes that support weight management during and beyond the medication period. LOSE WEIGHT WITH MEDICAL SUPPORT — BUILT FOR MEN Your personalised programme is built around medical care, not willpower. No generic diets. No guesswork. Just science-backed results and expert support. Find out if you’re eligible Take the quiz Learn more Step-by-Step Guide to Logging Meals While Taking Zepbound Establishing a consistent meal logging routine supports the therapeutic benefits of Zepbound while helping to monitor potential complications. Begin by selecting your tracking method before starting medication, whether a smartphone application, web-based platform, or paper journal. Consistency in the tracking tool facilitates pattern recognition and simplifies data review with healthcare providers. Daily logging protocol: Record immediately after eating rather than retrospectively, as delayed logging typically reduces accuracy Document all intake including beverages, condiments, cooking oils, and supplements that contribute calories or nutrients Note the time of consumption to identify relationships between meal timing and side effects or satiety patterns Rate hunger and fullness levels using a 1-10 scale before and after eating to track appetite changes Document any gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, bloating, or reflux associated with specific meals For portion estimation, use measuring cups and a digital food scale during the first few weeks to calibrate visual estimates. Most patients develop reasonable accuracy with practice, though periodic recalibration helps maintain consistency over time. Photograph meals as a backup verification method, particularly useful when dining out or eating unfamiliar foods. Schedule weekly reviews of your food logs, ideally on the same day each week. Look for patterns in protein intake, meal frequency, problematic foods, and correlation between eating patterns and side effects. Share these logs with your healthcare provider at each follow-up appointment, as this objective data informs dose adjustments and nutritional counseling. Importantly, contact your healthcare provider promptly if you experience severe or persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down for more than 24 hours, severe abdominal pain, or signs of dehydration such as dizziness or minimal urination. For individuals with a history of disordered eating, discuss the appropriate intensity of food tracking with your healthcare provider. Best Apps and Tools for Tracking Food on Zepbound Multiple digital platforms facilitate meal tracking for patients taking Zepbound, each offering distinct advantages. The following examples are provided for informational purposes only and do not constitute endorsements. MyFitnessPal features an extensive food database, barcode scanning capability, and restaurant menu integration. The free version provides comprehensive tracking, while premium features include advanced macronutrient analysis and meal planning tools. Its large user base means many foods are already cataloged, reducing manual entry time. Cronometer excels in micronutrient tracking, displaying detailed vitamin and mineral intake alongside macronutrients. This granular nutritional data proves particularly valuable for Zepbound patients at risk for deficiencies due to reduced food volume. The interface emphasizes nutritional completeness rather than simply calorie restriction. Cronometer's accuracy benefits from verified food data sources rather than user-generated entries. Lose It! offers an intuitive interface with photograph-based logging through its Snap It feature, which uses image recognition to identify foods and estimate portions. This functionality appeals to patients who find manual entry burdensome. The app integrates with fitness trackers and provides personalized calorie budgets, though these should be verified with your healthcare provider to ensure they align with clinical recommendations. For patients preferring simplicity, Baritastic was designed specifically for bariatric surgery patients but adapts well to GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy. It emphasizes protein tracking, hydration monitoring, and vitamin supplementation—priorities that mirror Zepbound nutritional management. The medication reminder feature helps maintain injection schedule adherence. Traditional paper journals remain valid alternatives for patients uncomfortable with technology or concerned about data privacy. Structured templates that prompt recording of time, food items, portions, and symptoms provide adequate documentation for clinical purposes. Note that most consumer health apps are not HIPAA-covered entities; review privacy policies before use. Regardless of platform, consistency matters more than sophistication—the best tracking tool is the one patients will actually use daily. What to Record: Nutrients, Portions, and Timing Comprehensive meal logging for Zepbound therapy extends beyond calorie counting to capture data essential for optimizing treatment outcomes and preventing complications. Protein intake requires particular attention, as inadequate consumption during rapid weight loss may accelerate lean muscle mass depletion. Work with your healthcare provider or registered dietitian to determine your individual protein needs, which typically range from 1.0-1.2 grams per kilogram of body weight daily during weight loss. Record protein sources at each meal, noting both quantity and quality—while many animal proteins provide complete amino acid profiles, several plant proteins (like soy and quinoa) are also complete, and others can be combined to improve amino acid balance. Macronutrient distribution should be documented to ensure balanced nutrition. While Zepbound reduces overall intake, maintaining adequate fat consumption (20-35% of calories per Dietary Guidelines for Americans) supports absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and hormone production. Complex carbohydrates from vegetables, whole grains, and legumes provide fiber essential for managing constipation, which can occur with Zepbound therapy. Track fiber intake explicitly, targeting 25-30 grams daily through food sources when possible. Portion sizes require accurate measurement, particularly for calorie-dense foods where small estimation errors significantly impact totals. Record portions in standard units (ounces, cups, tablespoons) rather than subjective terms like "small" or "medium." For mixed dishes, break down components when possible—a chicken stir-fry becomes 4 oz chicken, 1 cup vegetables, 2 teaspoons oil, ½ cup rice. Meal timing may influence medication tolerability and side effect profiles. Document the time of each eating occasion and note the interval since your Zepbound injection. Many patients find that adjusting meal timing and composition can help manage nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms. Record fluid intake separately from meals, as adequate hydration (about 2.7 liters daily for women and 3.7 liters daily for men from all sources, per National Academies guidelines) helps prevent dehydration. Finally, note any supplements including multivitamins, calcium, vitamin D, and vitamin B12, as deficiency risk may increase with restricted intake. Common Meal Logging Mistakes to Avoid on Zepbound Several systematic errors undermine the accuracy and utility of meal tracking for patients taking Zepbound. Underestimating portions represents the most prevalent mistake, with research demonstrating that individuals typically underreport calorie intake. This occurs through visual estimation errors, particularly for calorie-dense foods like oils, nuts, cheese, and nut butters where small volumes contain substantial calories. Use measuring tools consistently for these items, as a "handful" of almonds might vary significantly in calorie content depending on hand size and interpretation. Omitting beverages and condiments creates significant tracking gaps. Patients often forget to log cream in coffee, salad dressings, cooking oils, and caloric beverages, collectively contributing meaningful unrecorded calories daily. Similarly, "tastes" while cooking, finishing children's meals, or mindless snacking frequently go undocumented despite their caloric impact. If food enters your mouth, it belongs in your log. Inconsistent logging patterns diminish data utility. Recording only "good" days while omitting weekends or social occasions produces skewed information that misrepresents actual intake patterns. Healthcare providers need complete data to distinguish true medication non-response from dietary non-adherence. Similarly, abandoning logs after initial weight loss success prevents early detection of regain patterns. Focusing exclusively on calories while ignoring nutritional quality represents a critical error for Zepbound patients. A 1200-calorie diet of processed foods creates vastly different metabolic and health outcomes than 1200 calories of nutrient-dense whole foods. Track protein adequacy, micronutrient intake, and food quality alongside caloric totals. Failing to correlate symptoms with intake wastes valuable diagnostic information. When experiencing nausea, vomiting, or other gastrointestinal effects, note the specific foods consumed in the preceding hours. Patterns often emerge—high-fat meals, large portions, or specific trigger foods—enabling dietary modifications that improve tolerance. Share these correlations with your healthcare provider, as persistent symptoms may warrant dose adjustment or additional interventions. Importantly, contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience severe abdominal pain (especially if radiating to the back), persistent vomiting, signs of dehydration, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. These could indicate serious conditions requiring prompt medical attention. Remember that meal logging serves clinical purposes beyond weight monitoring; accurate, complete records optimize both safety and efficacy of Zepbound therapy. Frequently Asked Questions What should I track when logging meals on Zepbound? Track all food and beverage intake with accurate portions, protein content (targeting 1.0-1.2 grams per kilogram body weight daily), meal timing, hunger and fullness levels, fluid intake, and any gastrointestinal symptoms. Also document supplements and note correlations between specific foods and side effects to help optimize treatment. Which apps work best for tracking food while taking Zepbound? MyFitnessPal offers extensive food databases and barcode scanning, Cronometer excels at micronutrient tracking, Lose It! provides photo-based logging, and Baritastic emphasizes protein and hydration monitoring. The best app is whichever one you will use consistently daily, whether digital or a traditional paper journal. When should I contact my doctor about symptoms while on Zepbound? Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience severe or persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down for more than 24 hours, severe abdominal pain (especially if radiating to the back), signs of dehydration such as dizziness or minimal urination, or yellowing of skin or eyes. title: Gauzy Ltd. to Reschedule Third Quarter 2025 Earnings Release
summary: Gauzy - Gauzy Ltd. to Reschedule Third Quarter 2025 Earnings Release
body_text: Gauzy Ltd. to Reschedule Third Quarter 2025 Earnings Release Publisher: Global Newswire Discloses that Insolvency Proceedings Have Commenced Related to Certain French Subsidiaries Gauzy Adamantly Opposes the Proceedings and Plans to Appeal as Soon as Possible Gauzy Working with Its Lenders to Ensure Financial Viability of Its French Subsidiaries Gauzy Ltd. (Nasdaq: GAUZ) (“Gauzy” or the “Company”), a global leader in vision and light control technologies, today shared that it will not be releasing its financial results for the third quarter of 2025 on November 14 as previously planned. This postponement is unrelated to Gauzy’s third quarter performance. The Company will update the timing of release of its financial results as soon as practical. The reason for the delay is that, during a hearing held on November 13, 2025, the Commercial Court of Lyon, France, ordered the commencement of French law insolvency proceedings (“Redressement Judiciaire”) relating to three subsidiaries of Gauzy located in France. As is customary in such proceedings, the court ordered the appointment of two administrators and a creditor representative, responsible for advising the Company’s three subsidiaries in these proceedings. The Company strongly disagrees with the French court’s ruling and plans to have its subsidiaries appeal the decision of the court as soon as possible, while concurrently working collaboratively with the French administrators to quickly resolve the matter. The Company and its subsidiaries plan to continue normal operations as they seek to meet customer demand. Eyal Peso, Co-founder and CEO, commented, “Over the last three and a half years Gauzy has invested over $50 million in our people, assets, and operations in France. We fundamentally disagree with this decision, which we believe is unwarranted, and plan to appeal as soon as possible. Gauzy has immediately started working with the court appointed administrators to resolve this matter while ensuring business continuity for its employees, customers, and other valued stakeholders.” Background of Proceedings Redressement Judiciaire are French insolvency proceedings aimed at preserving a company’s business and operations, maintaining employment and repaying creditors while allowing for a plan to enable its recovery. Gauzy plans to have its subsidiaries appeal the decision to the Court of Appeal of Lyon as soon as possible and is currently working to ensure its subsidiaries have the financial means to meet their debts as they become due. However, pending this appeal, the insolvency proceedings will continue. Gauzy remains committed to complete transparency, and as such will provide updated information on these proceedings as soon as more information is available. About Gauzy Gauzy Ltd. is a fully-integrated light and vision control company, focused on the research, development, manufacturing, and marketing of vision and light control technologies that are developed to support safe, sustainable, comfortable, and agile user experiences across various industries. Headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, the company has additional subsidiaries and entities based in Germany, France, the United States, Canada, China, Singapore, and the United Arab Emirates. Gauzy serves leading brands across aeronautics, automotive, and architecture in over 60 countries through direct fulfillment and a certified and trained distribution channel. title: Data Center Power Insights: Q&A with Michelle McCarthy
summary: Plexus’ Michelle McCarthy discusses the rapid growth of the data center industry, critical power needs, key OEM challenges and emerging solutions.
body_text: Home Blogs Data Center Power Insights: Q&A with Michelle McCarthy Data Center Power Insights: Q&A with Michelle McCarthy Michelle McCarthy Sr. Director, Industrial Business Development • November 12, 2025 • 7 min read Designing | Servicing Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Share on Mail (Opens in new window) Mail Michelle McCarthy, Senior Director for Industrial Business Development at Plexus, leads a team that collaborates with original equipment manufactures (OEMs) to create custom design, manufacturing and servicing solutions for data center technologies. Plexus works with a broad range of OEMs across the power and energy landscape to build novel, reliable power infrastructure that data center operators rely on. From your recent engagement with companies, utilities and other stakeholders powering the data center market, what is your summary of the industry landscape today? The obvious answer is that the data center industry is experiencing rapid growth and expansion, with significant forecasts extending into 2030 and beyond. Currently, there are an estimated $2.7 trillion in active data center capital investment projects globally, according to Industrial Info Resources at the recent Data Center World POWER conference . North America accounts for the largest share with $1.8 trillion. Within the US, Texas is outpacing growth as compared to other states, while Northern Virginia remains a significant hub. This is followed by Europe with $421 billion, where the majority of development is taking place in the FLAP-D markets (Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Dublin). In the Asia Pacific region, projects total $411 billion. There is more limited development also happening in pockets of the Middle East and Latin America. The rapid pace of data center growth in the last two years can be attributed to several key factors: rapid AI developments and adoption, the widespread embrace of cloud computing and digital transformation, increasing digital content consumption, and the expansion of 5G networks and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Access to power is and will continue to be critical for data center developers. Developers and utilities must collaborate to meet rising power needs, emphasizing early planning for power and transmission to ensure continuity. Co-development, unique partnerships and overall collaboration are leading to new solutions and accelerating progress. Clean energy infrastructure is essential, with renewable energy being deployed at an unprecedented level. Solar still dominates renewables solutions, though technologies like geothermal, nuclear and offshore wind are rapidly following to meet increasing demand. It’s an energizing time to participate in the data center market. While there are real challenges, collaboration between grid operations, customers/hyperscalers, investors and policymakers is happening and will be paramount to deploy fast, scalable energy solutions to power economic development. What forward-looking solutions are gaining traction among utilities and OEMs responsible for data center power generation? Adopting flexible and resilient energy models will be crucial for sustainable growth. Investing in Behind the Meter (BTM) power, defined as power generation or storage on the customer’s side of the meter, is one such model. In the data center, operators are utilizing natural gas turbines, fuel cells, battery storage, solar, geothermal and small modular reactors (SMRs) for power and storage. These BTM solutions offer a competitive edge, protecting data center operators from grid power limitations and ensuring uptime standards are met. The industry recognizes that renewable energy resources will be imperative to meet data center energy needs going forward. More operators are using grid-scale batteries to help store and deploy energy to balance loads. These batteries are paired with wind and solar power solutions that can act as a ride through power supply in the face of grid interruptions. While traditional energy like natural gas continues to have a significant place, OEMs are recognizing that alternative energy sources will build resilience to continue to scale power generation for this explosive market. What concerns or constraints are top of mind for data center power OEMs, utilities and their customers, the developers and operators? Delays to builds are the number one concern, as lagging infrastructure and the rising costs to update or extend grids are impacting regions across the globe. This includes ongoing supply chain disruptions and constraints on key components like transformers and breakers, which can delay projects by years. In the US, permitting delays accelerate this challenge, and legislators are struggling to balance the demand for data center investment with the need to protect existing energy infrastructure. Texas is noted as a state with an advantage, as the Texas legislature has created the ability to fast-track growth and innovation in power generation by adapting laws and regulations to meet developer’s needs. Texas serves as a model for other jurisdictions interested in capturing more of this market. In Europe, operators and developers must navigate voluntary and mandatory regulations, such as the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact and EU Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements for energy usage for data centers. The focus on waste heat recovery, for example, is forcing innovative solutions such as integrating data center facilities with district heating networks to recapture and heat local communities. However, this requires strong existing infrastructure. A longer-term global concern exists with regard to overbuilding. As AI demand skyrockets, utilities face a dilemma: how to supply energy fast enough without overbuilding and risking stranded assets. In the US, for example, much of the electrical grid is seen to be in need of upgrades to meet demand. Traditional generation and transmission upgrades are slow and costly, which could risk US AI competitiveness. However, flexible on-site generation offers a solution to bridge this gap. Utilities and operators alike are leveraging and dispatching clean, on-site generation to unlock capacity using existing infrastructure, enhance grid reliability and accelerate digital infrastructure deployment. These are solutions that could be applied in all markets, regardless of infrastructure concerns, to establish localized and independent power supplies at the data centers. How can a partner like Plexus help the companies tackling these massive industry shifts meet their customer’s needs and capitalize on this moment of technological change? Data center developers and operators are currently focused on accelerating new builds, the reliability and quality of the power in their sites, and managing energy efficiency and operating costs. For OEMs serving these customers, having an electronic manufacturing services (EMS) partner can help overcome challenges in product development, manufacturing and servicing. This can ensure those OEMs can bring the highest quality infrastructure products to their data center customers and meet their significant expectations. Integrated engineering services to accelerate new product development Working with Plexus, an EMS company with robust engineering services, can help accelerate time-to-market on new product development. Plexus acts as an extension of our customer’s teams to partner on designing products throughout the data center. We also apply manufacturing experience to provide services like Design for Manufacturability and Design for Test. These solutions ensure a smooth transition from product design to new product introduction and into volume manufacturing. Plexus is also passionate about innovating responsibly as a sustainable business partner. We work with customers to develop sustainable products through services like Design for Environment and Life Cycle Assessment. These tools allow Plexus to help OEMs identify and quantify the carbon footprint of their products early in the design phase to reduce impact. The same processes can be applied to existing products to improve sustainability and decrease total cost of ownership. Global manufacturing for complex industrial products Plexus specializes in advanced manufacturing for high-power products. Our teams have extensive expertise manufacturing technologies in electrification, energy storage and energy management at the highest level of quality. Plexus’ product experience spans battery management systems, high-power battery chargers, power distribution units, uninterruptible power systems and beyond. At our ISO-certified global sites, end-to-end services from printed circuit board assembly to complex high level assembly are under one roof. Our global footprint also means customers access our worldwide Supply Chain Solutions to navigate global market dynamics and address their customers’ end markets with confidence. title: Task Batching Mastery: The Complete Productivity Playbook - Sunsama Blog
summary: Transform your productivity with proven task batching strategies. Learn from experts how to implement effective batching systems that eliminate distractions.
body_text: Why Task Batching Is Your Ultimate Productivity Game-Changer The infographic above illustrates how task batching can significantly improve your productivity. By implementing this technique, you can save an average of five hours each week, reduce context switching from 40 to 15 times per day, and increase overall productivity by 25% . These impressive statistics highlight the power of task batching for maximizing your work output. Understanding the Power of Focus Task batching isn't just another productivity fad; it's a fundamental shift in how you approach your work. Instead of constantly juggling different tasks, you group similar activities and dedicate specific time blocks to complete them. This approach fosters deep focus, minimizes distractions, and enhances efficiency. Think of it like meal prepping. You gather all your ingredients and prepare them in advance, rather than scrambling for each item as you need it. This streamlines the cooking process and saves valuable time. Task batching applies the same principle to your work, allowing you to operate with increased efficiency and focus. The Problem with Constant Task Switching This focused approach combats the negative effects of context switching , the act of shifting your attention between different tasks. Context switching disrupts focus and drains mental energy. Imagine writing an email, then attending a meeting, and then trying to resume writing. Each shift requires your brain to reorient, leading to productivity loss. Research from the American Psychological Association suggests that context switching can lead to a 40% decrease in productivity due to the mental lag involved in refocusing. Task batching helps prevent context switching by encouraging focused work on similar tasks within dedicated time blocks. This method minimizes mental fatigue and significantly improves inefficiency. To learn more, explore this in-depth article on task batching in Asana . To illustrate the differences between traditional task switching and the task batching approach, let's look at a comparison: Traditional Task Switching vs. Task Batching Approach A side-by-side comparison showing how different work approaches impact productivity and focus. This table clearly highlights the advantages of task batching. By consolidating similar tasks into dedicated time blocks, you achieve deeper focus, leading to increased productivity and reduced mental fatigue. The Benefits of Batching in Action Imagine dedicating a specific time block solely to email. Instead of scattering responses throughout the day and interrupting your flow, you handle them all at once. This concentrated effort boosts efficiency and reduces mental overhead. Batching also lets you leverage momentum. When you're in a state of flow, like writing, staying focused on writing-related tasks maintains that momentum. This immersive state allows for maximum productivity and higher quality output. By minimizing distractions and promoting sustained concentration, task batching allows you to accomplish more in less time, reducing stress and improving job satisfaction. The Real Cost Of Context Switching (And Why It's Killing Your Productivity) Building on the advantages of task batching, let's explore the downsides of its opposite: context switching . This seemingly harmless habit of juggling tasks throughout the day has a hidden cost, significantly impacting your overall productivity. You might be surprised to learn how much time and mental energy is wasted. The Illusion of Multitasking Many professionals believe they are effective multitaskers, capable of handling multiple tasks at once. However, research suggests this is often an illusion. Our brains aren't wired for true multitasking. Instead, we rapidly switch between tasks, incurring a context switching penalty each time. This penalty manifests as a mental lag, requiring time and energy to refocus. Imagine writing a report when an email notification pops up. You address the email and then return to your report. This brief interruption disrupts your flow, requiring you to re-establish your train of thought. This constant shifting diminishes productivity. For more insights, check out this article on How to master context switching . Quantifying the Productivity Loss The impact of context switching is backed by data. Statistics reveal that only 53.3% of work time is truly productive, largely due to interruptions and inefficient task switching. Task batching addresses this by grouping similar tasks, thus minimizing productivity loss. You can find more detailed statistics here . This means almost half of a typical workday is less effective due to distractions and constant task switching. This translates to lost time, missed deadlines, and increased stress. The cumulative effect of these small interruptions can significantly impact your overall performance and well-being. The Hidden Mental Energy Cost Beyond the quantifiable time lost, context switching also drains mental energy. Each shift in focus depletes mental resources, leading to fatigue and reduced cognitive function. This mental juggling can leave you feeling drained, even without completing much work. Furthermore, context switching hinders deep work . Complex tasks demand sustained focus. Constant interruptions prevent you from entering a flow state , where you are fully immersed and working at peak performance. This significantly impacts the quality and efficiency of output, especially for tasks requiring creativity or critical thinking. By understanding the real cost of context switching, you can appreciate task batching and its potential to unlock true productivity. Building Your Personal Task Batching System That Actually Works Context switching can really disrupt your workflow. Let's explore how to build a task batching system that works for you. This involves understanding your tasks, grouping them effectively, and organizing your schedule to boost your productivity. It might seem daunting initially, but a solid framework can make all the difference. Auditing Your Workday Begin by thoroughly examining your daily activities. List everything, from checking emails to attending meetings and working on projects. This helps uncover hidden patterns and areas where batching can be applied. You might find, for example, that you spend a lot of time scattered throughout the day answering emails. This fragmented approach can disrupt your focus on more demanding tasks. Consolidating email responses into dedicated blocks frees up mental space for more challenging activities. Identifying Natural Batching Opportunities After listing your tasks, look for natural groupings. Activities like writing or data analysis thrive on focused attention. Others, like responding to emails or making phone calls, are easily grouped together. Also, consider your energy levels. Schedule demanding tasks when you're most alert. Reserve less demanding tasks for periods of lower energy. This strategic approach maximizes productivity and prevents burnout. Tackle those challenging projects when you're at your peak, and handle less demanding tasks when your energy dips. Professionals using structured task batching systems report completing 67% more meaningful work daily, with 84% experiencing reduced stress and improved work-life balance. Learn more here. Creating a Batching Schedule Block out specific times for batched activities. Experiment with different time blocks. Some people prefer longer blocks for deep work, while others thrive on shorter, focused intervals. For example, dedicate two hours each morning to focused work on a specific project. Follow this with an hour for emails and administrative tasks. This minimizes distractions and promotes deep work. Structuring Your Batches Within each batch, prioritize strategically. Start with the most important or challenging activities while your energy is high. This ensures you tackle high-value work when you're best equipped to handle it. You might find this resource helpful: How to master productivity techniques . Building a successful task batching system takes experimentation and refinement. Be flexible. Adjust your approach based on your experiences. The key is finding a system that aligns with your work style and maximizes your productivity. Mastering Different Task Batching Categories For Maximum Impact Building a successful task batching system involves more than simply grouping similar tasks. It requires a deeper understanding of how different task categories interact within your workflow. This means recognizing which tasks complement each other and which require separate focus for optimal performance. Identifying Key Task Categories Most work activities fall into distinct categories, each with its own cognitive demands. Understanding these categories is the first step to effective batching. Communication: This includes activities like responding to emails, making phone calls, and engaging in instant messaging. Creative Work: This category encompasses tasks that require innovative thinking, such as writing, designing, and brainstorming. Administrative Tasks: These are often routine activities like data entry, filing, and scheduling. Decision-Making: This involves tasks that require critical thinking and analysis, such as project planning, strategy development, and problem-solving. Each category benefits from a specific batching strategy. For example, grouping communication tasks allows for efficient processing and quicker responses. However, combining creative work with administrative tasks can disrupt the focus needed for deep thinking. For more time management tips, check out this helpful guide: How to master various time management strategies . To help visualize the different categories and their optimal handling, let's look at a practical breakdown: In order to maximize focus and efficiency, it’s helpful to group similar activities together into dedicated time blocks. Below is a detailed overview of four key task categories—Communication, Creative Work, Administrative Tasks, and Decision-Making—along with recommended batch durations, optimal times of day, the tools you’ll need, and the metrics you can track to measure success. 1. Communication Batch Duration: 1–2 hours Best Time of Day: Mid-morning or late afternoon, when others are most responsive Tools Needed: Email client, Slack (or other chat apps), phone Success Metrics: Number of messages processed, average response time 2. Creative Work Batch Duration: 2–3 hours Best Time of Day: Morning or early afternoon, when your mind is freshest Tools Needed: Note-taking software (e.g. Evernote, OneNote), design tools (e.g. Figma, Adobe Creative Suite) Success Metrics: Number of ideas generated, projects moved to “draft” or “review” status 3. Administrative Tasks Batch Duration: 1–2 hours Best Time of Day: Late morning or early afternoon, when routine tasks feel least taxing Tools Needed: Project-management software (e.g. Asana, Trello), spreadsheets Success Metrics: Number of tasks closed, estimated time saved 4. Decision-Making Batch Duration: 1–2 hours Best Time of Day: During your personal peak-energy periods (often mid-morning or right after lunch) Tools Needed: Analytical tools, data dashboards (e.g. Tableau, Power BI) Success Metrics: Quality or accuracy of decisions, measurable impact on objectives (e.g. revenue uplift, cost savings ) This outlines how categorizing tasks, allocating specific time blocks, and utilizing appropriate tools can significantly impact productivity. By aligning these elements, you create a system for consistent and measurable success. Energy-Based Batching: Aligning Tasks with Your Natural Rhythms Effective task batching also involves understanding your energy levels. We all experience peaks and troughs in our energy throughout the day. Energy-based batching takes advantage of these fluctuations. Schedule demanding tasks like decision-making or creative work during your peak energy periods. Less demanding tasks, such as administrative duties or communication, can be reserved for lower energy times. This optimizes both performance and focus. Handling Urgent Interruptions and Maintaining Flexibility Unexpected interruptions are a common challenge with task batching. Emergencies and urgent requests are inevitable. However, they don't have to derail your system. Incorporate flexibility into your schedule. Include buffer time between batches to accommodate unforeseen tasks. This allows you to address urgent matters without disrupting your planned workflow. Examples of Effective Task Batching Strategies Here are some practical ways to implement task batching: Batch Similar Tasks: Group all writing-related tasks together, such as blog posts, reports, or email drafts. Theme Your Days: Dedicate specific days to certain types of work. For example, Mondays could be for project planning, while Wednesdays are for client communication. Timeboxing: Allocate specific time slots for different task categories to maintain focus and prevent overflow. By mastering the art of task categorization and scheduling, you transform task batching from a simple hack into a powerful system for maximizing your impact. Overcoming The Biggest Task Batching Challenges (Before They Derail You) Even the best-laid plans can encounter bumps in the road. Task batching, while incredibly effective, is no exception. This section explores common obstacles and offers practical advice to help you stay on course. From external disruptions to internal resistance, understanding these challenges is key to successful task batching. Dealing With Demanding Colleagues And Urgent Requests Interruptions from colleagues can be a major hurdle. Clearly communicating your task batching system to your team can significantly reduce disruptions. Explain when you're in focused work mode and when you're available for questions or collaboration. Setting clear communication boundaries is crucial. Let your team know specific times for checking emails and messages. This manages expectations and minimizes constant interruptions. Visual cues, like a "Do Not Disturb" sign or updated status on Slack , can also help. Managing Your Own Resistance To Structure Many people initially resist the structured approach of task batching. It can feel restrictive or unnatural at first. This resistance often stems from the fear of missing out on immediate responses or a perceived loss of flexibility. You might find helpful advice in this article: How to master overcoming procrastination . However, think of task batching as a tool to enhance your flexibility, not limit it. Start small. Implement task batching for one task category, like email management. Experience the benefits. As you become comfortable and see positive results, gradually expand the system to other work areas. Perfectionism And Procrastination: The Internal Saboteurs Perfectionism and procrastination can undermine your efforts. Perfectionists often struggle to begin tasks, fearing they won't be flawless. Procrastinators delay starting, disrupting the entire schedule. To combat these internal saboteurs, break large tasks into smaller, manageable parts. Focus on progress, not perfection. Celebrate small wins. This builds momentum and reduces overwhelm, making it easier to stay on schedule. Adjusting Your Approach When Things Don’t Go As Planned Task batching isn't a one-size-fits-all solution. Be ready to adapt and refine your approach. Track your progress and identify areas for improvement. For example, if tasks consistently take longer than allocated, adjust your time blocks. If certain task categories don't batch well together, try different combinations. The goal is to build a system that works for your style and maximizes your productivity. By addressing these challenges, you can transform task batching into a powerful productivity tool. Measuring Success And Optimizing Your 2.0 Task Batching Approach So you've implemented task batching. But how can you tell if it's truly effective? This section explores practical strategies for tracking your progress, evaluating your focus, and refining your approach without getting bogged down in complicated metrics. We'll focus on the indicators that truly matter, from completed tasks to your overall energy levels. Identifying Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Choosing the right metrics is essential for gauging the success of your task batching system. Instead of tracking every single detail, concentrate on key performance indicators (KPIs) that offer valuable insights. Completed Tasks: The simplest metric is the number of tasks you finish within each batch. This provides a clear picture of your output and overall efficiency. Time Spent on Each Batch: Keep track of the time you dedicate to each task category. This highlights how accurate your time estimations are and helps pinpoint potential bottlenecks. Focus Quality: While subjective, this metric is equally important. Reflect on how focused you were during each batch. Did you achieve a state of deep work, or were you easily distracted? Energy Levels: Pay attention to your energy levels throughout the day. Does task batching contribute to stable energy, or do you notice significant ups and downs? These KPIs offer a comprehensive perspective of your performance and highlight areas for improvement. Remember, quality over quantity is the key. It's not just about finishing tasks, but how effectively you work. Regularly Reviewing Your Task Batching System Consistency is crucial. Review your task batching system regularly. Weekly reviews are a good starting point. Analyze your KPIs and look for patterns. Are there certain task categories that consistently take longer than anticipated? Do your energy levels tend to drop at particular times? For example, if you consistently struggle with your creative tasks in the morning, consider shifting them to a later time when your energy is higher. Perhaps you're most productive in the afternoon. Adaptability is essential. You might be interested in: How to master daily planning . Making Data-Driven Adjustments Based on your reviews, make changes to your system. This might involve: Adjusting Time Blocks: If certain tasks regularly take longer than planned, adjust the allocated time blocks accordingly. Re-Categorizing Tasks: Experiment with different combinations; some tasks might be better suited to other categories. Refining Your Schedule: If you find your energy levels dipping at certain times, adjust your schedule to align demanding tasks with your peak energy periods. Optimizing Your Tools: The right tools can greatly improve your task batching. Consider using project management software or time tracking apps to streamline your process. Don't hesitate to experiment. Task batching is a personalized system that requires ongoing adjustments to suit your individual work style and demands. Evolving Your Approach as Your Work Changes Your work and priorities naturally evolve over time. Be flexible and adjust your task batching system accordingly. New projects, deadlines, and even personal commitments can affect your schedule and energy. Regularly reassess your tasks, categories, and schedule to make sure your system aligns with your current needs. This adaptability ensures task batching remains a valuable tool for long-term productivity. By consistently measuring, reviewing, and adapting, you create a sustainable system that grows with you. Key Takeaways Your journey to mastering task batching starts with understanding the core principles and putting them into practice. This section offers a roadmap, complete with actionable strategies and techniques you can use right away. We'll concentrate on building sustainable habits, monitoring your progress, and adapting your system as your needs change. Getting Started With Task Batching Identify Your Core Tasks: Start by making a list of all your regular activities. This gives you a clear overview of your workflow and highlights tasks you can batch. Categorize Similar Tasks: Group related tasks. This could include communication (email, messaging), creative work (writing, designing), administrative tasks, or decision-making activities. This categorization is the base of your batching system. Create a Schedule: Set specific times for each task category. Try different schedules to find what suits you best, whether it's longer blocks for focused work or shorter, more frequent intervals. Prioritize Within Batches: When your energy is highest, tackle the most important or challenging activities within each batch. This ensures you're doing high-value work when you're most alert. Setting Realistic Goals Start Small: Don't try to change everything at once. Begin with one task category, like email management, and gradually add more as you get comfortable. Focus on Consistency: Consistency is crucial for building habits. Even short, dedicated batching sessions are better than inconsistent efforts. Track Your Progress: Keep track of how much you complete within each batch. This gives you a clear measure of your productivity and helps you identify areas for improvement. Celebrate Small Wins: Acknowledge your achievements and celebrate milestones. This positive reinforcement helps you stay motivated. Maintaining Momentum and Troubleshooting Common Challenges Communicate Your Schedule: Let your team know your batching schedule to minimize interruptions during focus time. Handle Urgent Interruptions: Include buffer time in your schedule for unexpected requests and emergencies. Overcome Resistance: If you struggle with the structured approach of task batching, remember the benefits of increased focus and reduced stress. Combat Perfectionism and Procrastination: Divide large tasks into smaller, manageable steps to avoid feeling overwhelmed. Focus on making progress, not on being perfect. Scaling Your Task Batching System Regularly Review and Refine: Continuously review your system and make changes as needed. This keeps your approach effective as your work changes. Experiment With Different Batching Categories: As you get more practice, try different task combinations and time blocks to optimize your workflow. Integrate With Your Existing Tools: Use tools like project management software or time tracking apps to improve your process. Maintain Flexibility: Be ready to adapt your system as your work and priorities shift. The key is finding a balance between structure and flexibility. By following these key takeaways, you can create a task batching system that boosts your productivity, reduces stress, and helps you achieve more. title: How to book Air France First Class (La Première) using points
summary: Air France First Class is impossible to book with points alone, but there's a clever workaround.
body_text: How to book Air France First Class (La Première) using points By Tim Qin - Updated: June 25, 2026 Air France First Class is impossible to book with points alone, but there's a clever workaround. Photo Credit: Air France TLDR Only Flying Blue Platinum or Ultimate elite members can book Air France First Class (called La Première) directly using points. The cabin which costs around 200,000-300,000 Flying Blue miles . The work around is to book a business class award ticket using points, then upgrade with cash at check-in for around $1,500 to $2,500. An Air France first class seat regularly sells for $10,000 to $20,000, but can pay 60,000 points for business class plus $1,500-$3,000 for the upgrade. Step 1: Book Air France business class with points Flying Blue has a published tool that lets you price out the lowest possible miles prices for entry fares. Using this tool, we can see that Europe award flights to/from the contiguous 48 United States, Canada, and Mexico all cost 45,000 to 60,000 points one way when flying on Air France or KLM. Alternative, you can search for Air France award flight deals using the Roame reward flight finder . Air France La Premiere. Credit: Air France Step 2: Upgrade to Air France First Class Now here's where it gets interesting. Air France sometimes offers paid upgrades from business class to first class, including on award tickets. This is most commonly available at check-in, though expect it to be pricey. Upgrade costs will rarely be as low as $1,000, and it's much more common to see upgrade offers in the $1,500-3,500 range. Timing is everything The magic window opens 30 hours before departure. That's when Air France releases unsold La Première seats for upgrades. Just log in to Flying Blue, go to "My Travel," go to your booking, and check for upgrade offers. This may require multiple tries, so make sure to check on all four channels: the Air France app and website as well as we the KLM app and website. Upgrade pricing patterns Based on recent data points from travelers: Paris to Dubai: ~$1,500 to $1,900 Paris to Los Angeles: ~$2,500 to $3,200 Paris to Miami: ~$2,300 Paris to New York: ~$2,600 Paris to SAn Francisco: ~$3,000 Important restriction As of July 1, 2023, Air France has implemented a policy whereby you can no longer upgrade business class award tickets to first class. However, this policy has been inconsistently enforced, and many travelers report still receiving upgrade offers at check-in. Your mileage may vary. La Première routes Not every Air France flight has La Première. Air France exclusively has its La Premiere first class cabin on around two dozen Boeing 777-300ERs, operating select long haul flights out of Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG). Current La Première routes from Paris (CDG) With new La Première suites: Atlanta (ATL) - AF30/AF31 Los Angeles (LAX) - AF20/AF21, AF22/AF23 Miami (MIA) - AF90/AF91 New York (JFK) - AF4/AF3 and AF6/AF5. All JFK flights to feature the new suites by July 2026. title: Unlocking a $230B Enterprise Opportunity: How an Early-Stage AI Company Expanded into Regulated Markets with Omnistrate
summary: Autoblocks used Omnistrate to evolve from a serverless cloud product into an enterprise-ready SaaS platform, enabling secure, compliant, customer-controlled deployments.
body_text: At-a-Glance Autoblocks used Omnistrate to evolve from a serverless cloud product into an enterprise-ready SaaS platform, enabling secure, compliant, customer-controlled deployments. Company Autoblocks, a growth stage company, helps product teams to collaboratively evaluate, test, and improve their GenAI/LLM products. Category AI Application Testing & Validation Platform Challenge Enterprise buyers in regulated industries such as healthcare and finance were highly interested in Autoblocks but required strict data control and compliance — limiting its ability to sell into those markets. Result With Omnistrate, Autoblocks stood up an enterprise SaaS delivery platform in weeks (vs. ~12 months DIY), enabling flexible customer-managed deployments of the Autoblocks workspace including BYOC and on-prem environments —and unlocking access to an estimated $230B in regulated-industry AI budgets. The Challenge Enterprise Demand for Safe, Compliant Deployments Autoblocks helps companies develop and validate AI applications before they reach production. Its platform enables teams to simulate real-world scenarios, evaluate model behavior, and continuously improve AI performance with real-world scenarios and subject matter expert (SME) feedback. Autoblocks had validated market traction, but scaling to enterprise buyers revealed four major friction points: Data Residency & Compliance Distributing Autoblocks software to Healthcare and financial customers with regional data residency controls to meet HIPAA and GDPR mandates. AI Infrastructure Complexity Managing GPU orchestration, CUDA environments, and third-party AI integrations (e.g., Amazon Bedrock) across clouds demanded scale that a small team couldn't support. Operational Burden Each enterprise install required manual, bespoke DevOps support, slowing sales and consuming engineering time. Monetization & Visibility Lacking built-in usage tracking and billing, Autoblocks couldn't measure cost efficiency or expansion metrics investors wanted to see. "Very early on, prospects were asking if they could run Autoblocks in their own cloud. Before Omnistrate, supporting that was a non-starter; now it's a pretty simple check the box." — Adam Nolte Co-Founder & CTO, Autoblocks The Solution Omnistrate's SaaS Control Plane To meet enterprise demand for secure, customer-controlled deployments, Autoblocks needed a scalable way for customers to run its AI testing platform within their own cloud environments. Rather than building this complex infrastructure from scratch, Autoblocks partnered with Omnistrate. Autoblocks used Omnistrate's powerful Agentic Control Plane as a Service to power the Autoblocks Deployment Portal — a self-service environment where enterprise customers can deploy, manage, and monitor Autoblocks directly in their own cloud infrastructure, all with centralized visibility and automated lifecycle management. Secure, Customer-Managed Deployments Enabled Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) and on-prem deployments so enterprises can run Autoblocks entirely within their own environments — ensuring data sovereignty, security, and compliance. AI-Native Infrastructure Support Delivered GPU orchestration, CUDA support, and Amazon Bedrock integrations to power high-performance AI workloads with fast model startup and scaling. Unified Operations Layer Centralized monitoring, upgrades, and lifecycle management — giving Autoblocks' DevOps and security teams a unified operations layer and single point of control across all customer environments. Integrated Billing & Marketplace Readiness Delivered built-in usage metering and per-tenant cost insights, automated invoicing, and AWS Marketplace integration — giving Autoblocks full visibility into resource economics while enabling usage-based pricing and faster enterprise monetization through cloud marketplaces. "For a small team at our stage, [ building out that control plane infrastructure] would have taken up all of our time. So Omnistrate was a pretty clear decision. Now we're spending all of our time actually building and iterating on our product." — Adam Nolte Co-Founder & CTO, Autoblocks The Impact Accelerated Market Readiness and Enterprise Growth Through Omnistrate, Autoblocks evolved from a cloud-only application into an enterprise-ready SaaS with global deployment flexibility. With these advancements, Autoblocks is positioned for sustainable scale: a leaner operating model, faster enterprise onboarding, and an adaptable architecture that aligns with the growing compliance requirements across AI-driven sectors. Weeks to Enterprise Deployments Omnistrate's control-plane-as-a-service cut deployment timelines by over 80%, moving from concept to production in weeks instead of a year. Sales and Adoption Acceleration Built-in BYOC options turned regulatory barriers into an Autoblocks differentiator, streamlining security reviews, building trust and accelerating deal closure. Operational Efficiency Automation and centralized observability reduced DevOps overhead by half, enabling engineering teams to reinvest capacity into product innovation. Expanded Addressable Market Secure, compliant deployments unlocked access to an estimated $230 billion regulated-industry AI market. "We can say 'hey yeah we offer BYOC! We have a complete portal where you can deploy Autoblocks into your VPC with just a few clicks.'" — Adam Nolte Co-Founder & CTO, Autoblocks Enterprise Opportunity Expanding into High-Growth Regulated Markets With Omnistrate, Autoblocks unlocked access to two of the fastest-growing AI markets, healthcare and financial services, where strict compliance and data-control requirements have historically slowed adoption. Omnistrate’s secure, customer-managed deployment model positioned Autoblocks to confidently sell into these high-value, compliance-sensitive sectors — transforming data governance and control into a competitive advantage. The AI in Healthcare market is projected to grow from $26.5B in 2024 to over $187B by 2030 (CAGR ~39%) . The AI in Financial Services market is expected to rise from $45B in 2024 to nearly $100B by 2027 . Estimated at $230B Total in 2025 Why Omnistrate Why Autoblocks Chose Omnistrate Autoblocks selected Omnistrate based on four critical evaluation criteria: speed to market, regulatory compliance, enterprise scalability, and trusted technical expertise. By adopting Omnistrate's control-plane-as-a-service, Autoblocks accelerated regulated-market entry, reduced infrastructure overhead, and positioned its platform for scalable, secure expansion in enterprise AI testing and validation. Unified control across environments Omnistrate provided a build-once, run-anywhere control plane for customer-managed deployments across AWS, GCP, and Azure—spanning BYOC , on-prem, and even air-gapped—so enterprises keep data sovereignty and operational control. Compliance and observability built in The platform's SOC 2 Type II controls , integrated billing, and end-to-end observability delivered turnkey enterprise-grade operations that met the strict standards of regulated sectors. AI-native infrastructure Omnistrate's GPU orchestration, CUDA compatibility, and native integrations with AI services such as Amazon Bedrock enabled Autoblocks to deliver high-performance workloads to enterprise customers. Proven enterprise partnership Omnistrate's leadership team brought a track record of innovation in control-plane design and software distribution, underpinned by more than fifty patents across infrastructure awareness, data management, and orchestration technologies.
